html:
SMTO-LLM-0081 — An older thinking limit stopped this answer

GUID: 1a65768a-47bf-4808-be15-bc2112718a23
Slug: model-reasoning-budget-exceeded
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • An older SMTO version stopped the model when it thought longer than its thinking target. SMTO now treats that target as a guide and lets the model keep thinking. Work already finished was kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure SMTO has been updated and restarted, then open the stopped task and select Resume. Current SMTO lets the model keep thinking past the target, so the same step can now finish.
  2. Leave Thinking target (%) and the thinking switch as they are. The target no longer stops answers, so changing it would only change how much the model is encouraged to think.
  3. If the answer is still cut off, open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card and Limits and recovery, raise Output allowance, select Save Main, and start a new task. The model's overall output limit still applies, and a resumed task keeps the limit it started with.

What success looks like

  • The resumed task continues past the step that stopped before, with at most a notice about the thinking target.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't carry out the step's half-written action yourself; SMTO discarded it on purpose, and don't keep retrying the same rejected step unchanged.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An older runtime rejected the decision when the model's reasoning exceeded the Thinking target (%) share of its output allowance; current runtimes treat that percentage as a soft target that only produces a notice.

What this means

  • An older runtime rejected this decision when reasoning crossed its percentage allowance. Current runtimes treat that percentage as a soft target and continue productive thinking. Explicit provider output limits still apply.

Why this can happen

  • A historical runtime enforced the thinking percentage as a hard limit.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the runtime version and event timestamp. Current soft-target notices are informational and do not discard thinking.

How to fix it

  • Resume the task on the current version; no setting change is required, because Thinking target (%) is now a soft target that emits a once-per-decision notice and never rejects output. Explicit provider output limits (Output allowance) and the Force budget and stop thinking option still apply, and the discarded partial tool call must not be executed.
  • Resume the task on the updated runtime. Raising the thinking percentage or switching thinking off is not required to pass the soft target.

Retry and execution caution

  • Explicit Resume starts a fresh episode and retains completed tool receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Productive reasoning continues beyond the soft target within explicit provider and task resource limits.

What not to do

  • Do not execute incomplete tool arguments or repeatedly retry the same rejected decision.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
